details.description: Unauthorized rideshare when subway is under 15 minutes

audit_output.audit_summary: The expense claim for the $28.00 Uber ride has been rejected. Under SEC-2.1, rideshares are non-reimbursable when public transit is under 15 minutes. The employee documented that public transit takes 9 minutes, and no eligible exceptions under SEC-2.2 applied.

judge.judge_critique: The auditor's decision is fully grounded in the provided policy framework and matches the ground truth outcome exactly. audit_output.audit_summary: The expense report is rejected due to policy violations under SEC-4.1 and SEC-4.2. details.description: Excessive hotel room rate exceeding tier limit

Book standard single-room corporate rates within policy limits for future travel.

citations.title: Lodging Rate Limits
citations.relevant_clause: Hotel accommodations must be booked at standard single-room corporate rates. Maximum allowable room rates: Tier 1 Cities (New York, San Francisco, London, Tokyo): $300.00 / night (pre-tax). All Other Cities: $200.00 / night (pre-tax).

judge.judge_critique: The auditor's assessment is completely accurate and aligned with the ground truth policy. details.description: Client entertainment exceeding $150 per person limit

violations.description: Client entertainment meal expense exceeded the maximum allowable cap of $150.00 per attendee (inclusive of food, tax, and tip).
violations.evidence: Submitted dinner expense at Per Se totaled $455.00 for 2 documented attendees ($227.50 per person), exceeding the $300.00 maximum allowed for 2 people.

remediation_steps: Acknowledge the policy deduction of $155.00 for exceeding the per-person client entertainment spending cap.
Re-submit expense report reflecting the approved reimbursement total of $300.00 ($150.00 per attendee cap), or obtain executive exception approval for the overage.

citations.title: Per-Person Spending Cap
citations.relevant_clause: Client entertainment meals are subject to a maximum cap of $150.00 per attendee (inclusive of food, drinks, tax, and tip). Spending exceeding $150.00 per person will have the excess amount disallowed.
citations.explanation: The total receipt of $455.00 for 2 documented attendees exceeds the maximum allowed reimbursement of $300.00 ($150.00 per person) by $155.00.

audit_output.audit_summary: The expense report contains valid business justification and attendee documentation, and tip was compliant at 20%. However, the dinner total of $455.00 for 2 attendees ($227.50 per person) violates the strict $150.00 per attendee limit under SEC-3.2. Consequently, $155.00 is disallowed, and $300.00 is approved.

judge.judge_critique: The auditor accurately identified the policy cap violation under SEC-3.2. The calculation is exact: 2 attendees allow up to $300.00, resulting in a disallowed amount of $155.00 on the $455.00 claim. The remediation instructions are courteous, actionable, and clearly present standard pathways (adjusting the total to the cap or seeking an executive exception).

details.description: Split receipt evasion on same day at same restaurant totaling over per diem

violations.description: Total meal expenditures on 2026-10-04 exceeded the strict $75.00 daily per diem cap for individual business travel meals.
violations.evidence: Receipts REC-21A ($54.50) and REC-21B ($49.00) on 2026-10-04 total $103.50, exceeding the $75.00 daily cap by $28.50.

violations.description: A single dinner transaction at Luigi's Trattoria was split into two consecutive receipts within 45 minutes.
violations.evidence: Submitted REC-21A ($54.50 at 19:15 for appetizer/pasta) and REC-21B ($49.00 at 20:00 for entree/dessert) from the same venue on the same evening.

remediation_steps: Acknowledge the $75.00 daily meal per diem cap and refrain from splitting single dining transactions into multiple receipts.
Resubmit the claim reflecting the allowable $75.00 reimbursement cap for the day.

citations.title: Daily Per Diem Limit
citations.relevant_clause: Individual business travel meals are subject to a strict $75.00 daily per diem cap per calendar day. Any cumulative meal expenditure exceeding $75.00 on a single day is non-reimbursable for the excess amount. Consecutive receipts on the same calendar day must be combined when assessing the $75.00 limit.
citations.explanation: Both dinner receipts from 2026-10-04 aggregate to $103.50, exceeding the daily per diem limit by $28.50.

citations.title: Artificial Receipt Splitting
citations.relevant_clause: Intentionally splitting a single transaction into multiple smaller receipts is considered a policy violation. Audits must aggregate all receipts from the same vendor or within the same meal timeframe.
citations.explanation: Two separate receipts were generated for courses of the same dinner at the same restaurant 45 minutes apart.

audit_output.audit_summary: The expense report was rejected due to an artificial receipt split at Luigi's Trattoria and an excess over the daily meal per diem limit. The receipts on 2026-10-04 aggregate to $103.50, exceeding the $75.00 daily cap. Reimbursement is limited to $75.00, resulting in $28.50 disallowed.

judge.judge_critique: The auditor flawlessly detected both the intentional split transaction and the per diem cap overage. The specific sections (SEC-1.1 and SEC-5.1) are accurately cited, the math correctly disallows $28.50 while approving up to the $75.00 threshold, and the remediation guidance provides clear, constructive steps for the employee to resubmit their claim compliant with policy.

citations.title: Alcohol Policy
citations.relevant_clause: For eligible dinners, total alcohol charges (including beer, wine, cocktails, and liquor) must not exceed 20% of the meal subtotal (pre-tax, pre-tip). Any alcohol expenditure exceeding the 20% cap is disallowable and will be deducted from the reimbursement total.
citations.explanation: Alcohol accounted for $30.00 of the $70.00 subtotal (42.86%), which exceeds the 20% threshold of $14.00.

citations.title: Daily Per Diem Limit
citations.relevant_clause: Individual business travel meals are subject to a strict $75.00 daily per diem cap per calendar day. Any cumulative meal expenditure exceeding $75.00 on a single day is non-reimbursable for the excess amount.
citations.explanation: The total dinner receipt of $91.00 exceeded the daily maximum meal allowance of $75.00.

audit_output.audit_summary: The expense report violates SEC-1.2 (Alcohol Policy) and SEC-1.1 (Daily Per Diem Limit). judge.judge_critique: The auditor accurately identified the disguised alcohol line item, applied the correct 20% subtotal limit ($14.00 cap on a $70.00 meal subtotal), and accurately disallowed $16.00.
